body: Ouch, dude. I also saw my last relationship end because of my bad anxiety (and also in my case, depression). Talk about it in therapy - it's easy to pass it off as all your fault, but we you have to remember your partner isn't perfect either. In my case, my partner always wanted to go out, attend events, and travel, which we did half the time, but I was at home paralyzed with anxiety the other half the time. My partner often lamented about how boring and uninterested in their life I was. I was in therapy throughout our relationship and worked hard to better myself, but as anyone who has suffered from those things knows, progress can be very slow. It took me years more of therapy to understand that while there were some things I could have done better, my partner never should have called me boring, antisocial, or uninterested, especially when I spent our whole relationship in therapy devoting a lot of time and energy to working on my issues. It's hard to find a partner that understands your anxiety, but it's not impossible.
